### ARCHITECTURE.md
# Architecture Design

## System Overview
Pi Network Marketplace - a frontend-only prototype simulating a decentralized marketplace where Pioneers buy/sell goods and services using Pi cryptocurrency. Includes simulated Pi SDK authentication, payment flows, subscription management, and multi-language support.

## Tech Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript
- Vite build tool
- shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS
- React Router v6
- Tanstack React Query

## Module Design
| Module | Responsibility | Key Files |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| Pi SDK Simulation | Auth, payments, user management | src/lib/pi-sdk.ts |
| Store | State management, cart, products data | src/lib/store.ts |
| i18n | Multi-language support (EN/FR/ES/ZH/AR) | src/lib/i18n.ts |
| Navigation | App-wide navbar with auth/cart/language | src/components/Navbar.tsx |
| Homepage | Hero, stats, categories, featured products | src/pages/Index.tsx |
| Marketplace | Product grid with search/filter/sort | src/pages/Marketplace.tsx |
| Product Detail | Single product view with payment | src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx |
| Cart | Shopping cart with Pi checkout | src/pages/Cart.tsx |
| Subscriptions | Plans with smart contract info | src/pages/Subscriptions.tsx |
| Profile | User stats, transactions, reputation | src/pages/Profile.tsx |
| Seller | Dashboard with listings management | src/pages/Seller.tsx |

## Tech Decisions
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| No real Pi SDK | Simulated SDK layer | Prototype phase, no mainnet access |
| Frontend-only | No backend needed | All data is mock/simulated |
| Simple state | Module-level state with listeners | Lightweight, no Redux needed |
| Multi-language | Custom i18n with 5 languages | Simple, no heavy library needed |

## File Tree Plan
```
src/
├── lib/
│   ├── pi-sdk.ts          # Pi Network SDK simulation
│   ├── store.ts           # State, products, cart, transactions
│   └── i18n.ts            # Internationalization
├── components/
│   ├── Navbar.tsx          # Navigation bar
│   ├── Footer.tsx          # Footer
│   └── ProductCard.tsx     # Reusable product card
├── pages/
│   ├── Index.tsx           # Homepage
│   ├── Marketplace.tsx     # Product listing
│   ├── ProductDetail.tsx   # Single product
│   ├── Cart.tsx            # Shopping cart
│   ├── Subscriptions.tsx   # Plans
│   ├── Profile.tsx         # User profile
│   └── Seller.tsx          # Seller dashboard
└── App.tsx                 # Routes
```

## Implementation Guide
The Pi SDK simulation layer mirrors the real @pinetwork-js/sdk API structure (init, authenticate, createPayment) with simulated delays and mock data. The subscription page references the PiRC2 Soroban smart contract design for recurring payments. All payments simulate the full flow: pending → server approval → completion.

# Architecture Design

## System Overview
Pi Network Marketplace - a frontend-only prototype simulating a decentralized marketplace where Pioneers buy/sell goods and services using Pi cryptocurrency. Includes simulated Pi SDK authentication, payment flows, subscription management, and multi-language support.

## Tech Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript
- Vite build tool
- shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS
- React Router v6
- Tanstack React Query

## Module Design
| Module | Responsibility | Key Files |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| Pi SDK Simulation | Auth, payments, user management | src/lib/pi-sdk.ts |
| Store | State management, cart, products data | src/lib/store.ts |
| i18n | Multi-language support (EN/FR/ES/ZH/AR) | src/lib/i18n.ts |
| Navigation | App-wide navbar with auth/cart/language | src/components/Navbar.tsx |
| Homepage | Hero, stats, categories, featured products | src/pages/Index.tsx |
| Marketplace | Product grid with search/filter/sort | src/pages/Marketplace.tsx |
| Product Detail | Single product view with payment | src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx |
| Cart | Shopping cart with Pi checkout | src/pages/Cart.tsx |
| Subscriptions | Plans with smart contract info | src/pages/Subscriptions.tsx |
| Profile | User stats, transactions, reputation | src/pages/Profile.tsx |
| Seller | Dashboard with listings management | src/pages/Seller.tsx |

## Tech Decisions
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| No real Pi SDK | Simulated SDK layer | Prototype phase, no mainnet access |
| Frontend-only | No backend needed | All data is mock/simulated |
| Simple state | Module-level state with listeners | Lightweight, no Redux needed |
| Multi-language | Custom i18n with 5 languages | Simple, no heavy library needed |

## File Tree Plan
```
src/
├── lib/
│   ├── pi-sdk.ts          # Pi Network SDK simulation
│   ├── store.ts           # State, products, cart, transactions
│   └── i18n.ts            # Internationalization
├── components/
│   ├── Navbar.tsx          # Navigation bar
│   ├── Footer.tsx          # Footer
│   └── ProductCard.tsx     # Reusable product card
├── pages/
│   ├── Index.tsx           # Homepage
│   ├── Marketplace.tsx     # Product listing
│   ├── ProductDetail.tsx   # Single product
│   ├── Cart.tsx            # Shopping cart
│   ├── Subscriptions.tsx   # Plans
│   ├── Profile.tsx         # User profile
│   └── Seller.tsx          # Seller dashboard
└── App.tsx                 # Routes
```

## Implementation Guide
The Pi SDK simulation layer mirrors the real @pinetwork-js/sdk API structure (init, authenticate, createPayment) with simulated delays and mock data. The subscription page references the PiRC2 Soroban smart contract design for recurring payments. All payments simulate the full flow: pending → server approval → completion.

## 📋 **Résumé Exécutif**

**EcoChain AI** est une application Android décentralisée sur **Pi Network** qui permet à chaque utilisateur de **monétiser ses données environnementales** (qualité de l'air, consommation énergétique, empreinte carbone, données météo locales) via l'IA prédictive, tout en participant à un **marché mondial de la donnée climatique** régi par des smart contracts. L'utilisateur **gagne des Pi** en partageant ses données anonymisées, et l'IA génère des **prédictions climatiques personnalisées** avec une précision inégalée.

> *"La première bourse mondiale de données environnementales, sécurisée par la blockchain, amplifiée par l'IA, accessible à tous via Pi Network."*

---

## 🌍 **Concept Détaillé**

### **Problème résolu**
- Les données environnementales sont **monopolisées** par les gouvernements et les grandes entreprises
- Les citoyens **ne sont pas rémunérés** pour leurs données locales
- La recherche climatique manque de **données diversifiées et en temps réel**
- Les prédictions climatiques sont **coûteuses et inaccessibles** au grand public

### **Solution**
EcoChain AI crée un **écosystème circulaire** :

```
Utilisateur → Données environnementales anonymisées → IA prédictive → Score écologique + Prédictions
                ↓
        Récompenses en Pi (tokenomics)
                ↓

### **SDK Pi**
```javascript
// Auth
Pi.init({ version: "2.0", sandbox: true });
const user = await Pi.authenticate(["username", "payments"]);

// Paiements
const payment = await Pi.createPayment({
  amount: 10,
  memo: "EcoChain AI Premium - 1 Month",
  metadata: { productId: "premium_monthly" }
}, {
  onReadyForServerApproval: (paymentId) => approvePayment(paymentId),
  onReadyForUserApproval: (paymentId) => showApproval(paymentId),
  onCancel: (paymentId) => handleCancel(paymentId),
  onError: (error) => handleError(error)
});
```

- ✅ Sandbox → Mainnet progressif
- ✅ Paiements via Pi uniquement
- ✅ Aucune crypto externe
- ✅ Données stockées sur IPFS (décentralisé)
- ✅ UI adaptée Pi Browser

schemas.description: A tool for reading, understanding, writing, and editing files. Support local file including text-based files (txt, md, json, py, html, js, css, etc.), pdf, docx, excluding images, csv, excel, or online links. Note: Editor.read does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately via attach_medium_by_paths. For agent: Do NOT initiate multiple Editor.insert_content_at_line calls at the same time, since the line number will change starting with the first execution, making line number of the subsequent calls incorrect. Split the calls into separate responses. For the same reason, Editor.insert_content_at_line should NOT go behind Editor.edit_file_by_replace in the same response. Perform insert operation in a separate response.

edit_file_by_replace.description: Edit a file. This will search for `old_string` in the given file and replace it with `new_string`. Every *old_string* must *EXACTLY MATCH* the existing source code, character for character, including all comments, docstrings, etc. * The `old_string` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces! * If the `old_string` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_string` to make it unique * The `new_string` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_string` For example, given a file "path/to/example.txt" with the following content: ``` line 1 line 2 line 2 line 3 ``` EDITING: If you want to replace the second occurrence of "line 2", you can make `old_string` unique: edit_file_by_replace( 'path/to/example.txt', old_string='line 2 line 3', new_string='new line line 3', ) This will replace only the second "line 2" with "new line". The first "line 2" will remain unchanged. The resulting file will be: ``` line 1 line 2 new line line 3 ``` REMOVAL: If you want to remove "line 2" and "line 3", you can set `new_string` to an empty string: edit_file_by_replace( 'path/to/example.txt', old_string='line 2 line 3', new_string='', )
edit_file_by_replace.signature: (self, path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str) -> str

read.description: Read the whole content of a file, or a line range when line arguments are provided. Using an absolute path as the argument for specifying the file location. For large text/source files, prefer partial reads, e.g. start_line=1, max_lines=500 or start_line=500, end_line=800. Note: This method does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately.
read.signature: (self, path: str, start_line: Optional[int] = None, end_line: Optional[int] = None, max_lines: Optional[int] = None) -> metagpt.tools.libs.editor.FileBlock

similarity_search.description: Given a filename or a pathname, performs a similarity search for a given query across the specified file or path. This method searches the index repository for the provided query, classifying the specified files or paths. It performs a search on each cluster of files and handles non-indexed files separately, merging results from structured indices with any direct results from non-indexed files. This function call does not depend on other functions.
similarity_search.parameters: Args: query (str): The search query string to look for in the indexed files. path (Union[str, Path]): A pathname or filename to search within. Returns: List[str]: A list of results as strings, containing the text from the merged results and any direct results from non-indexed files. Example: >>> query = "The problem to be analyzed from the document" >>> file_or_path = "The pathname or filename you want to search within" >>> texts: List[str] = await Editor.similarity_search(query=query, path=file_or_path) >>> print(texts)

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS scores_user_idx ON scores(user_id); ... CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS scores_score_idx ON scores(score DESC); ... ... -- Setup Row Level Security (RLS) ... ALTER TABLE scores ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ... CREATE POLICY "allow_read_all_scores" ON scores FOR SELECT USING (true); ... ''' >>> result = await create_tables(sql) # Create storage bucket with RLS policies >>> bucket_sql = ''' ... BEGIN; ... -- Create storage bucket ... CREATE POLICY "allow_users_upload_own_profile" ON storage.objects FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'profile_pictures' AND (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text); ... COMMIT; ... ''' >>> bucket_result = await create_tables(bucket_sql)

schemas.description: A tool for reading, understanding, writing, and editing files. Support local file including text-based files (txt, md, json, py, html, js, css, etc.), pdf, docx, excluding images, csv, excel, or online links. Note: Editor.read does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately via attach_medium_by_paths. For agent: Do NOT initiate multiple Editor.insert_content_at_line calls at the same time, since the line number will change starting with the first execution, making line number of the subsequent calls incorrect. Split the calls into separate responses. For the same reason, Editor.insert_content_at_line should NOT go behind Editor.edit_file_by_replace in the same response. Perform insert operation in a separate response.

read.description: Read the whole content of a file. Using an absolute path as the argument for specifying the file location. Note: This method does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately.

similarity_search.description: Given a filename or a pathname, performs a similarity search for a given query across the specified file or path. This method searches the index repository for the provided query, classifying the specified files or paths. It performs a search on each cluster of files and handles non-indexed files separately, merging results from structured indices with any direct results from non-indexed files. This function call does not depend on other functions.
similarity_search.parameters: Args: query (str): The search query string to look for in the indexed files. path (Union[str, Path]): A pathname or filename to search within. Returns: List[str]: A list of results as strings, containing the text from the merged results and any direct results from non-indexed files. Example: >>> query = "The problem to be analyzed from the document" >>> file_or_path = "The pathname or filename you want to search within" >>> texts: List[str] = await Editor.similarity_search(query=query, path=file_or_path) >>> print(texts)

This method searches the index repository for the provided query, classifying the specified files or paths. It performs a search on each cluster of files and handles non-indexed files separately, merging results from structured indices with any direct results from non-indexed files. This function call does not depend on other functions.
similarity_search.parameters: Args: query (str): The search query string to look for in the indexed files. path (Union[str, Path]): A pathname or filename to search within. David.task_type_desc:
- **eda**: For performing exploratory data analysis
- **data preprocessing**: For preprocessing dataset in a data analysis or machine learning task ONLY,general data operation doesn't fall into this type
- **feature engineering**: Only for creating new columns for input data.
- **model train**: Only for training model.
- **model evaluate**: Only for evaluating model.
- **image2webpage**: For converting image into webpage code.
- **other**: Any tasks not in the defined categories

- **web scraping**: For scraping data from web pages.
- **email login**: For logging to an email.

schemas.description: A tool for browsing the web. Don't initialize a new instance of this class if one already exists. Note: If you plan to use the browser to assist you in completing tasks, then using the browser should be a standalone task, executing actions each time based on the content seen on the webpage before proceeding to the next step. ## Example Issue: The details of the latest issue in the geekan/MetaGPT repository. Plan: Use a browser to view the details of the latest issue in the geekan/MetaGPT repository. Every *to_replace* must *EXACTLY MATCH* the existing source code, character for character, including all comments, docstrings, etc. * The `to_replace` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces! * If the `to_replace` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `to_replace` to make it unique * The `new_content` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `to_replace` For example, given a file "path/to/example.txt" with the following content: ``` line 1 line 2 line 2 line 3 ``` EDITING: If you want to replace the second occurrence of "line 2", you can make `to_replace` unique: edit_file_by_replace( 'path/to/example.txt', to_replace='line 2 line 3', new_content='new line line 3', ) This will replace only the second "line 2" with "new line". The first "line 2" will remain unchanged. The resulting file will be: ``` line 1 line 2 new line line 3 ``` REMOVAL: If you want to remove "line 2" and "line 3", you can set `new_content` to an empty string: edit_file_by_replace( 'path/to/example.txt', to_replace='line 2 line 3', new_content='', )

# Architecture Design

## System Overview
Pi Network Marketplace - a frontend-only prototype simulating a decentralized marketplace where Pioneers buy/sell goods and services using Pi cryptocurrency. Includes simulated Pi SDK authentication, payment flows, subscription management, and multi-language support.

## Tech Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript
- Vite build tool
- shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS
- React Router v6
- Tanstack React Query

## Module Design
| Module | Responsibility | Key Files |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| Pi SDK Simulation | Auth, payments, user management | src/lib/pi-sdk.ts |

## Tech Decisions
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| No real Pi SDK | Simulated SDK layer | Prototype phase, no mainnet access |
| Frontend-only | No backend needed | All data is mock/simulated |
| Simple state | Module-level state with listeners | Lightweight, no Redux needed |
| Multi-language | Custom i18n with 5 languages | Simple, no heavy library needed |

## Current User Requirement
Faire un **audit complet** de PoliGov pour vérifier que tout fonctionne correctement, et s’assurer que le **pseudo Pi Network apparaît automatiquement dès que l’utilisateur clique “Se connecter Pi”** (sur mobile).

## Total Summary
Vous avez construit une application web de gouvernance (initialement PiDAO/PiPolis, renommée puis **PoliGov/PolisGo**) avec pages: propositions/votes/commentaires, financement, dashboard, escrow, réputation, quêtes, admin, i18n (dont arabe RTL), animations, puis intégration progressive Pi (SDK/API simulée puis câblage backend). Ensuite vous avez demandé l’alignement Pi Develop et un contrôle du bon fonctionnement/login.

## Files
- **User-provided**
  - ` /workspace/uploads/FEUILLE_DE_ROUTE_PIPOLIS_30JOURS.docx` : feuille de route 30 jours (inspiration pour le plan d’amélioration)
  - ` /workspace/uploads/paste-text.txt` (et variantes) : texte/points à intégrer dans votre feuille de route (référence pour “e”)
  - ` /workspace/uploads/pirc2` (dossier) : ressources PiRC2 à aligner côté app
  - ` /workspace/uploads/sdk` (dossier) : ressources Pi SDK
  - ` /workspace/uploads/smartcontract` (dossier) : références smart contract
  - ` /workspace/uploads/DEVELOPMENT_ROUTE_*` (si présent dans le contexte via uploads) : non explicitement listé, mais vous avez insisté sur conformité aux normes Pi Develop / Pi Browser.
  - ` /workspace/uploads/1779677350224.jpeg` : logo fourni (mise à jour logo)

- **Criteru/crucial côté projet**
  - ` /workspace/.atoms/PROGRESS.md` : suivi détaillé des phases, renommages, intégrations et checklists
  - ` /workspace/.atoms/ARCHITECTURE.md` : architecture tech stack (frontend React/TS, etc.)

- **Fichiers écrits/édités (d’après le log)**
  - ` /workspace/.atoms/PROGRESS.md` : mise à jour répétée (renommages Polis/PiPolis/PolisGo→PoliGov, ajout pages, statuts, intégrations)
  - Frontend (ensemble du dossier présent dans le commit, notamment):
    - ` /workspace/app/frontend/src/components/` : `Navbar.tsx`, `LanguageSelector.tsx`, `NotificationBell.tsx`, `PiPaymentButton.tsx`, `GlobalSearch.tsx`, etc.
    - ` /workspace/app/frontend/src/pages/` : `Proposals.tsx`, `ProposalDetail.tsx`, `CreateProposal.tsx`, `Funding.tsx`, `Dashboard.tsx`, `Quests.tsx`, `Escrow.tsx`, `Admin.tsx`, `ApiDocs.tsx`, `Security.tsx`, `Reputation.tsx`, etc.
    - ` /workspace/app/frontend/src/lib/` : `pi-sdk.ts`, `auth.ts`, `api.ts`, `i18n.ts`, etc.
  - Backend (ensemble du dossier présent dans le commit, notamment):
    - ` /workspace/app/backend/routers/` : `pi_auth.py`, `pi_payments.py`, `votes.py`, `governance.py`, `quests.py`, etc.
    - ` /workspace/app/backend/services/` : `pi_profiles.py`, `payment.py`, `votes.py`, etc.
    - ` /workspace/app/backend/main.py`, ` /workspace/app/backend/core/*`, modèles ` /workspace/app/backend/models/*`
  - Assets/branding:
    - ` /workspace/app/frontend/public/assets/*` et ` /workspace/app/frontend/dist/assets/*` : logos `logo-poligov.jpeg`, et autres variantes (selon historique)

## Completed Tasks
- Construction et itérations successives de l’app, avec renommages:
  - PiDAO → PiPolis → Polis → PolisGo → **PoliGov** (final)
- Pages principales construites et connectées au backend (selon PROGRESS):
  - Propositions, détail + vote, financement, dashboard utilisateur, création de proposition
  - Commentaires/discussion
  - Quêtes + suivi/claim
  - Escrow `/escrow/:id`
  - Réputation `/reputation`
  - Admin dashboard `/admin`
  - Délégation votes `/delegation`
  - Analytics `/analytics`, carte projet `/map`
- i18n multi-langues avec **arabe RTL**, et pages légales:
  - `Privacy` / `Terms` en plusieurs langues dont AR
- UX:
  - animations fluides (fade-in/slide-up), transitions page
  - performance: lazy loading / Suspense, skeletons/pagination (selon PROGRESS)
- Intégrations Pi (progressives):
  - wrapper/flow auth & payments “Pi SDK” puis câblage backend (selon log)
- Déploiement/preview (indiqué par build et prerender dans le log):
  - `pnpm run build` a prerender ` /` et `/blog/`
- Ajouts docs:
  - pages `/api-docs` et `/security`

## Ongoing Tasks
- **Audit fonctionnel complet** de PoliGov
  - Vérifier que toutes les routes/pages/services fonctionnent sans erreur (ex: erreurs de route `/api/v1/entities/votes/all?limit=1` déjà rencontrées auparavant)
- **Auto-détection du pseudo Pi Network au clic “Se connecter Pi”**
  - Problème actuel: le pseudo n’apparaît pas automatiquement (déjà rapporté: “mon pseudo pi n’est pas encors detecté”)

    - Frontend: `Pi.authenticate` / callback / récupération identifiant
    - Backend: route(s) `pi_auth` / vérification token `/v2/me` et persistance `pi_profiles`
    - Affichage Navbar: champs `@username`
- Aucun **ID de tâche** explicite n’a été fourni dans votre demande (donc je n’en invente pas).

### ARCHITECTURE.md
# Architecture Design

## System Overview
Pi Network Marketplace - a frontend-only prototype simulating a decentralized marketplace where Pioneers buy/sell goods and services using Pi cryptocurrency. Includes simulated Pi SDK authentication, payment flows, subscription management, and multi-language support.

## Tech Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript
- Vite build tool
- shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS
- React Router v6
- Tanstack React Query

## Module Design
| Module | Responsibility | Key Files |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| Pi SDK Simulation | Auth, payments, user management | src/lib/pi-sdk.ts |
| Store | State management, cart, products data | src/lib/store.ts |
| i18n | Multi-language support (EN/FR/ES/ZH/AR) | src/lib/i18n.ts |
| Navigation | App-wide navbar with auth/cart/language | src/components/Navbar.tsx |
| Homepage | Hero, stats, categories, featured products | src/pages/Index.tsx |
| Marketplace | Product grid with search/filter/sort | src/pages/Marketplace.tsx |
| Product Detail | Single product view with payment | src/pages/ProductDetail.tsx |
| Cart | Shopping cart with Pi checkout | src/pages/Cart.tsx |
| Subscriptions | Plans with smart contract info | src/pages/Subscriptions.tsx |
| Profile | User stats, transactions, reputation | src/pages/Profile.tsx |
| Seller | Dashboard with listings management | src/pages/Seller.tsx |

## Tech Decisions
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| No real Pi SDK | Simulated SDK layer | Prototype phase, no mainnet access |
| Frontend-only | No backend needed | All data is mock/simulated |
| Simple state | Module-level state with listeners | Lightweight, no Redux needed |
| Multi-language | Custom i18n with 5 languages | Simple, no heavy library needed |

## File Tree Plan
```
src/
├── lib/
│   ├── pi-sdk.ts          # Pi Network SDK simulation
│   ├── store.ts           # State, products, cart, transactions
│   └── i18n.ts            # Internationalization
├── components/
│   ├── Navbar.tsx          # Navigation bar
│   ├── Footer.tsx          # Footer
│   └── ProductCard.tsx     # Reusable product card
├── pages/
│   ├── Index.tsx           # Homepage
│   ├── Marketplace.tsx     # Product listing
│   ├── ProductDetail.tsx   # Single product
│   ├── Cart.tsx            # Shopping cart
│   ├── Subscriptions.tsx   # Plans
│   ├── Profile.tsx         # User profile
│   └── Seller.tsx          # Seller dashboard
└── App.tsx                 # Routes
```

## Implementation Guide
The Pi SDK simulation layer mirrors the real @pinetwork-js/sdk API structure (init, authenticate, createPayment) with simulated delays and mock data. The subscription page references the PiRC2 Soroban smart contract design for recurring payments. All payments simulate the full flow: pending → server approval → completion.

ARCHITECTURE.md.System Overview: Pi Network Marketplace - a frontend-only prototype simulating a decentralized marketplace where Pioneers buy/sell goods and services using Pi cryptocurrency. Includes simulated Pi SDK authentication, payment flows, subscription management, and multi-language support.
ARCHITECTURE.md.Tech Decisions:
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| No real Pi SDK | Simulated SDK layer | Prototype phase, no mainnet access |
| Frontend-only | No backend needed | All data is mock/simulated |
| Simple state | Module-level state with listeners | Lightweight, no Redux needed |
| Multi-language | Custom i18n with 5 languages | Simple, no heavy library needed |

Reserved for the case where the next question genuinely depends on the current answer — do not chain ``ask`` calls in one round to fake batching. - ``ask_batch(questions=[...])`` —— Mike-initiated MULTI-item card (one QuestionCard with paginated Next/Back). Use whenever you have ≥2 independent clarification questions in the same think round. Mixed kinds (single / multi / open) are allowed in the same items[] array. For scenario-driven plan modules (features_* / theme_select), keep using ``PlanComposer.run`` — that's a separate scenario tool, not for ad-hoc clarifications.

ask.description: Ask the user a SINGLE clarification question and wait for their answer. Use this only when the next question's text genuinely depends on this question's answer (i.e., you cannot batch them in advance). For 2+ independent questions in one round, call ``ask_batch`` instead.
ask.parameters: Args: prompt: The question text shown to the user — a SINGLE concise question line. Do NOT append a hint about single vs multiple choice (e.g. ``(可多选)``, ``(多选)``, ``(单选)``, ``(multiple choice)``, ``(single choice)``, ``(choose all that apply)`` or any variant). The frontend renders the choice-mode hint automatically from ``kind``; duplicating it produces a doubled "(可多选) (multiple choice)" suffix in the UI. Also: NEVER pack multiple questions into this single ``prompt`` using numbered lists ("1. ... 2. ... 3. ..."), semicolons, or "and also tell me ..." — each ``ask`` is one question. kind: One of ``clarification_single`` / ``clarification_multi`` / ``clarification_open``. Other kinds (``features_*`` / ``theme_select``) belong to ``PlanComposer`` and must NOT be used here. options: List of ``{option_id, label, description?, is_default?}``. Required for ``clarification_single`` / ``clarification_multi``; ignored for ``clarification_open``. Do NOT include an "Other / 其他 / Other (please describe) / 其他（请描述）" entry here — when ``allow_custom_input=true`` the frontend renders a built-in custom-input row, and listing "Other" as a regular option produces two "Other" rows. scenario_family: Optional scenario tag (analytics only). stage: One of ``plan_clarify`` / ``plan_modules`` / ``post_plan_clarify``. Defaults to ``post_plan_clarify`` (stage A or C); callers in stage B can override to ``plan_clarify``. allow_custom_input: Whether to allow an "Other" free-text row. If users might want a free-form answer, set this to True instead of adding an "Other" option to ``options[]``. question_id: Optional override; auto-generated if omitted. title: Card header text. Returns: dict: AnswerPayload (or ``{"timeout": True, "card_id": ...}`` on 24h no-response, or ``{"error": ...}`` on push failure).
ask.signature: (self, prompt: str, kind: str = 'clarification_open', options: Optional[list[dict]] = None, scenario_family: str = '', stage: str = 'post_plan_clarify', allow_custom_input: bool = True, question_id: Optional[str] = None, title: str = 'Questions') -> dict

ask_batch.description: Ask the user MULTIPLE independent clarification questions in ONE multi-item card with Next/Back pagination. Use this whenever you have ≥2 clarification questions to ask in the same think round and the questions are independent (each one's text does NOT depend on another's answer). Mixed kinds are allowed — ``clarification_single`` / ``clarification_multi`` / ``clarification_open`` items can coexist in the same card. Compared with ``PlanComposer.run``: PlanComposer is a scenario-driven action that internally regenerates the scenario's default modules (features / theme); it is NOT a generic batch tool and calling it repeatedly will re-emit the same scenario questions. Use ``ask_batch`` for any ad-hoc batch (post-Decline replanning beyond the scenario default, post-plan deep-dive clarification, multiple unrelated questions in stage A, etc.).
ask_batch.parameters: Args: questions: A list of question dicts. Each dict must include: - ``prompt`` (str, required): single-line question text. Same rules as ``ask.prompt`` — no choice-mode suffix, one question per prompt. - ``kind`` (str, optional, default ``clarification_open``): one of ``clarification_single`` / ``clarification_multi`` / ``clarification_open``. - ``options`` (list[dict], optional): same shape as ``ask.options`` — ``[{option_id, label, description?, is_default?}]``. Required for ``_single`` / ``_multi``, ignored for ``_open``. - ``allow_custom_input`` (bool, optional, default True): same semantics as ``ask.allow_custom_input``. - ``required`` (bool, optional, default True). - ``question_id`` (str, optional): auto-generated if omitted. scenario_family: Optional scenario tag (analytics only). stage: One of ``plan_clarify`` / ``plan_modules`` / ``post_plan_clarify``. Defaults to ``post_plan_clarify``. title: Card header text. Returns: dict: AnswerPayload — ``{"card_id", "answers": [...], "submit_action"}`` where ``answers[i]`` corresponds to ``questions[i]`` in the same order. Or ``{"timeout": True, "card_id": ...}`` on 24h no-response, or ``{"error": ...}`` on push failure.
ask_batch.signature: (self, questions: list[dict], scenario_family: str = '', stage: str = 'post_plan_clarify', title: str = 'Questions') -> dict

schemas.description: A tool for reading, understanding, writing, and editing files. Support local file including text-based files (txt, md, json, py, html, js, css, etc.), pdf, docx, excluding images, csv, excel, or online links. Note: Editor.read does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately via attach_medium_by_paths. For agent: Do NOT initiate multiple Editor.insert_content_at_line calls at the same time, since the line number will change starting with the first execution, making line number of the subsequent calls incorrect. Split the calls into separate responses. For the same reason, Editor.insert_content_at_line should NOT go behind Editor.edit_file_by_replace in the same response. Perform insert operation in a separate response.

glob.description: Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size. - Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts" - Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time (most recently modified first) - Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
glob.parameters: Args: pattern: The glob pattern to match files against (e.g. "**/*.tsx"). path: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

grep.description: A powerful search tool built on ripgrep. Usage: - ALWAYS use `Editor.grep` for search tasks. NEVER invoke `grep` or `rg` as a Terminal.run command. - Supports full regex syntax (e.g., "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+") - Filter files with glob parameter (e.g., "*.js", "**/*.tsx") or type parameter (e.g., "js", "py", "rust") - Output modes: "content" shows matching lines, "files_with_matches" shows only file paths (default), "count" shows match counts - Pattern syntax: Uses ripgrep (not grep) - literal braces need escaping (use `interface\{\}` to find `interface{}` in Go code) - Multiline matching: By default patterns match within single lines only. For cross-line patterns like `struct \{[\s\S]*?field`, use `multiline: true`
grep.parameters: Args: pattern: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents. path: File or directory to search in. Defaults to current working directory. glob: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob. output_mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts. Defaults to "files_with_matches". context_before: Lines before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content". context_after: Lines after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content". context: Lines before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content". line_number: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true. case_insensitive: Case insensitive search (rg -i). type: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. head_limit: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content limits output lines, files_with_matches limits file paths, count limits count entries. Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited; use sparingly because large result sets waste context. offset: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit. Defaults to 0. multiline: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall).
grep.signature: (self, pattern: str, path: str = '.', glob: Optional[str] = None, type: Optional[str] = None, output_mode: str = 'files_with_matches', line_number: bool = True, case_insensitive: bool = False, context_before: int = 0, context_after: int = 0, context: int = 0, multiline: bool = False, head_limit: Optional[int] = None, offset: int = 0) -> str

read.description: Read the whole content of a file, or a line range when line arguments are provided. Using an absolute path as the argument for specifying the file location. For large text/source files, prefer partial reads, e.g. start_line=1, max_lines=500 or start_line=500, end_line=800. Note: This method does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately.
read.signature: (self, path: str, start_line: Optional[int] = None, end_line: Optional[int] = None, max_lines: Optional[int] = None) -> metagpt.tools.libs.editor.FileBlock

similarity_search.description: Given a filename or a pathname, performs a similarity search for a given query across the specified file or path. This method searches the index repository for the provided query, classifying the specified files or paths. It performs a search on each cluster of files and handles non-indexed files separately, merging results from structured indices with any direct results from non-indexed files. This function call does not depend on other functions.
similarity_search.parameters: Args: query (str): The search query string to look for in the indexed files. path (Union[str, Path]): A pathname or filename to search within. Returns: List[str]: A list of results as strings, containing the text from the merged results and any direct results from non-indexed files. Example: >>> query = "The problem to be analyzed from the document" >>> file_or_path = "The pathname or filename you want to search within" >>> texts: List[str] = await Editor.similarity_search(query=query, path=file_or_path) >>> print(texts)

ask_human.description: Use this when you fail the current task or if you are unsure of the situation encountered. Your response should contain a brief summary of your situation, ended with a clear and concise question.

Use this when you have a clear answer or solution to the user's question. **NEVER** mention internal `.atoms/` context files (e.g., ATOMS.md, PROGRESS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md) or any bare `filename.ext` in reply_to_human. collect_secret.description: Analyze the draft plan to identify required API keys/secrets for third-party services. Check if existing secrets fulfill the needs, otherwise suggest keys from the key list. This tool is also the standard entrypoint to trigger the platform UI to confirm and persist secrets. Do not assume chat-pasted secrets are already saved for deployment/runtime. Call this function after draft_plan approval if the development plan involves any third-party services or APIs (e.g., email sending, cloud storage, authentication providers, etc.). IMPORTANT INPUT RULE: - Incremental requests: call ONLY when a new 3rd-party service/API or new key/secret is introduced. - If key/service names are not in the plan, append them to `draft_plan_content` under "UserProvidedSecretHints" (names only). Backend-aware routing: use collect_secret ONLY when a backend has been activated for this project (the key is injected at runtime and read by the backend). For a pure-frontend project with no activated backend — where the key is used directly in the browser — use request_secret instead.
collect_secret.parameters: Args: draft_plan_content: The development plan content summary with all the functionalities/features mentioned. If needed, append a short "UserProvidedSecretHints" section with key/service NAMES ONLY (no values). Returns: str: JSON containing: - available_keys: Keys already in secret manager that can be used - required_keys: Keys that need to be obtained (with service, description, access_model, guide) - not_found: Features needing to find suitable APIs - summary: Brief summary for the main agent

request_secret.description: According to the user's needs, determine whether a third-party KEY is required to achieve the requirement, supplement the required SECRET information, and let the user fill in the format
request_secret.parameters: Args: secret_info (list[dict]): Contains multiple Secrets, each Secret includes the name and description of the Key. dict object must contain `KEY_NAME` and `KEY_DESC` fields. Returns: None Example: secret_info = [{"KEY_NAME": "PIXABAY_API_KEY", "KEY_DESC": "The API Key For Image Searching Engine Pixabay"}]

schemas.description: A role who can think and act dynamically

draft_plan.description: Present a development plan to human for confirmation before distributing tasks to team members. When to call: - The requirement is non-trivial (multi-page, stateful, involves complex interactions, or integrates multiple services) and benefits from confirming scope first. - The requirement is genuinely ambiguous and you need human clarification. When to SKIP (assign directly with "Plan confirmed, proceed directly"): - The task is trivial and single-purpose (e.g. hello world, snake game, static homepage, basic calculator, personal business card, simple demo, PPT, data dashboards). - The requirement is clear and unambiguous with an obvious implementation path.
draft_plan.parameters: Args: content: A string containing numbered plan items (e.g., "1. Task A\n2. Task B\n3. Task C") Returns: str: The human's response/confirmed plan, or error message if format is incorrect

publish_team_message.description: Publish a message to a team member, use member name to fill send_to args. Team members keep public conversation context in memory, but only direct assignments trigger their work. Keep content concise and actionable: specify the task, essential constraints, key references, plan state, and required setup/tool constraints. Avoid pasting the original content verbatim unless exact wording matters. Do not mention default stack/tooling choices unless the user asks for them or a specific template/tool is required.

schemas.description: A tool for running terminal commands. Don't initialize a new instance of this class if one already exists.

run.description: Executes a specified command in the terminal and streams the output back in real time. The Primary Project workspace is the stable workspace root. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh). Terminal.run commands that use `cd` will change the current shell directory for subsequent commands, including later turns. IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user: - File search: Use `Editor.glob` (NOT find or ls) - Content search: Use `Editor.grep` (NOT grep or rg) - Read files: Use `Editor.read` (NOT cat/head/tail) - Edit files: Use `Editor.edit_file_by_replace` (NOT sed/awk) - Write files: Use `Editor.write` (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF) While this tool can do similar things, the dedicated tools provide a better experience and clearer tool calls. # Instructions - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location. - Avoid unnecessary `cd`. If you are already in the correct project directory, run commands there directly. When you need to run a command in another project directory, prefer command directory flags or absolute paths when available. - Prefer relative paths from the current shell directory when applicable; avoid unnecessarily repeating absolute project paths. Good style: the search target is under the current shell directory (`app`), so `path` is relative: <Editor.glob> <pattern> **/*.tsx </pattern> <path> frontend/src </path> </Editor.glob> Bad style: `path` repeats the redundant absolute path even though `backend` is already inside `app` <Editor.glob> <pattern> **/models/photos.py </pattern> <path> /x/y/z/absolute/path/to/project/app/backend </path> </Editor.glob>
run.parameters: Args: cmd (str): The command to execute in the terminal. Returns: str: The command's output.

schemas.description: A tool for reading, understanding, writing, and editing files. Support local file including text-based files (txt, md, json, py, html, js, css, etc.), pdf, docx, excluding images, csv, excel, or online links. Note: Editor.read does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately via attach_medium_by_paths. For agent: Do NOT initiate multiple Editor.insert_content_at_line calls at the same time, since the line number will change starting with the first execution, making line number of the subsequent calls incorrect. Split the calls into separate responses. For the same reason, Editor.insert_content_at_line should NOT go behind Editor.edit_file_by_replace in the same response. Perform insert operation in a separate response.

find_file.description: Finds all files with the given name or path in the specified directory.
find_file.parameters: Args: file_name: str: The name or path of the file to find. If it's an absolute path, will match the exact path. If it's a relative path, will match the path suffix. If it's just a name, will match file names. dir_path: str: The path to the directory to search.

read.description: Read the whole content of a file. Using an absolute path as the argument for specifying the file location. Note: This method does NOT support reading image files (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tiff). Image files are handled separately.

schemas.description: Plan is a sequence of tasks towards a goal.

append_task.description: Append a new task with task_id (number) to the end of existing task sequences. If dependent_task_ids is not empty, the task will depend on the tasks with the ids in the list. Note that the assignee should be the 'name' of the role.

finish_current_task.description: Finish current task, set Task.is_finished=True, set current task to next task

replace_task.description: Replace an existing task (can be current task) based on task_id, and reset all tasks depending on it.

reset_task.description: Reset a task based on task_id, i.e. set Task.is_finished=False and request redo. This also resets all tasks depending on it.
reset_task.parameters: Args: task_id (str): The ID of the task to be reset.

schemas.description: A role who can think and act dynamically

ask_human.description: Use this when you fail the current task or if you are unsure of the situation encountered. Your response should contain a brief summary of your situation, ended with a clear and concise question.

reply_to_human.description: Reply to human user with the content provided. Use this when you have a clear answer or solution to the user's question.

schemas.description: SEO content generation agent. See SEO_INSTRUCTION for workflow details.

draft_plan.description: Present SEO content matrix to user for confirmation before generating files. This tool provides a structured interaction for users to review and approve the SEO content plan. It automatically handles the user confirmation flow.
draft_plan.parameters: Args: content: Numbered list of SEO pages (format: "1. Page A 2. Page B 3. Page C") Each line should describe a planned SEO page from the generated matrix. preselect_count: Number of pages to pre-select in UI (default: 5, set 0 for none) Returns: str: Parsed user response with approval status and selected pages User response options: - approve_all: Generate all pages in the plan - approve: Generate only specific selected pages (provide page numbers) - update: Request modifications to the plan (provide feedback) Note: This tool automatically pauses execution and waits for user input. Do NOT call <end></end> after this tool - it handles the wait internally.

generate_markdown_batch.description: Generate markdown files for all approved SEO pages in batch. This tool handles the entire Step 3 workflow: filters approved pages from seo_matrix, generates images, creates markdown content using writer_llm, and writes files.
generate_markdown_batch.parameters: Args: status: Approval status from draft_plan. One of: - "APPROVE_ALL": Generate all pages in seo_matrix - "APPROVE": Generate only selected pages - "UPDATE": User wants to modify plan (do not call this tool) selected_tasks: List of 1-based task indexes to generate (only used when status="APPROVE"). Example: [1, 3, 5] means generate pages 1, 3, and 5 from seo_matrix. lang: Language code for YAML frontmatter. Default: "zh" Returns: str: Generation summary with success/failure counts and file paths

generate_seo_outline.description: Generate comprehensive SEO content matrix outline. This tool creates a complete SEO content strategy with page titles, URL paths, target keywords, and content outlines for each page.
generate_seo_outline.parameters: Args: topic: Main topic/product for SEO content (e.g., "Task Management Application") keywords: Comma-separated list of core keywords (optional, extracted if not provided) num_pages: Number of pages to generate in matrix (default: 20) categories: Comma-separated page categories to cover (default: standard SEO categories) Returns: JSON string containing complete SEO matrix: - topic: Topic summary - total_pages: Number of pages generated - pages: Array of page objects with title, url_path, keywords, category, outline
generate_seo_outline.signature: (self, topic: 'str', keywords: 'str' = '', num_pages: 'int' = 20, categories: 'str' = 'Core Features,Product Features,Use Cases,Pain Points,Comparisons,Education,FAQ') -> 'str'

set_project_context.description: Save project context gathered from Step 1 scan for use in Step 3 markdown generation. This tool stores structured project information that will be injected into each markdown article to ensure consistent internal linking and accurate project references.
set_project_context.parameters: Args: project_summary: Brief description of the project (features, target audience, value props). Example: "A task management app for teams with real-time collaboration, Kanban boards, and time tracking features." routes: List of route objects with path and description. Include CTA routes like /signup, /pricing, /demo for article CTAs. Example: [{"path": "/dashboard", "description": "Main dashboard"}, {"path": "/signup", "description": "User registration"}, {"path": "/pricing", "description": "Pricing plans"}] theme_summary: Summary of theme tokens, layout system, and visual style to inherit. Returns: str: Confirmation message with stored context summary

schemas.description: A tool for running terminal commands. Don't initialize a new instance of this class if one already exists.

run.description: Executes a specified command in the terminal and streams the output back in real time.
run.parameters: Args: cmd (str): The command to execute in the terminal. Returns: str: The command's output.

schemas.description: Web search engine tool

run.signature: (self, query: str, flag: str = 'deep search') -> list[dict]
